newsitem.title: CHINA: China to import 7.0 mln tonnes of grain in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China to import 7.0 mln tonnes of grain in 1996.

text.p: China will import 7.0 million tonnes of grain in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
Total demand for grain was expected to be 470 million tonnes this year, Xinhua said.

State purchases of grain in January-September were 53 million tonnes, 9.7 million tonnes more than the same period in 1995, the agency said. A portion of state grain purchases go into government stores.
China had stockpiled more than 128 million tonnes of grain by end-September, a rise of 31 million tonnes from September 1995, it said.
Grain prices rose 7.9 percent in January-September, an increase less than that in the same 1995 period, it said.
Western industry analysts have estimated China would need to import about 8.0 million tonnes of wheat this year following its bumper harvest.
Chinese agricultural officials have said China's grain demand will rise to nearly 500 million tonnes in the year 2000 and to 550 million tonnes by 2010.
China's grain output was estimated at 480 million tonnes this year, up nearly 15 million tonnes from 1995's record harvest.
